summary: A Done top-level row whose figures moved after it settled now reads "Name  (revised)". The mark comes from a new init-only TopLevelRow.Revised, and the tracker sets it in the way the accepted M2 finding decided: each row records (Bytes, OnDisk) when its pending count reaches 0 (FolderExited, or Seed for file rows). Build then latches Revised whenever it builds a Done row whose figures differ from that record. Moved itself is unchanged, so every writer of a row's figures is covered. TopLevelRowText.TitleOf gains the one Done-when-Revised case. The three declared fitness rules are replaced by the two structural ones the review decided (M3, m2, m3). A design-as-built record (docs/design/SL-063-done-row-revised.md) holds the M1/M4 structural reasons and the restated key decision 5. The acceptance command now exits 0 (10/10), the full default Core.Tests suite passes (381/381) and Fitness holds all 61 rules. The shipped exe runs end to end on a repro tree, and a real C:\Windows scan through Core and the converter marked no rows.

files.why: Adds TopLevelRow.Revised (bool, init-only, default false). Rewrites the TopLevelState.Done doc to say what Done actually promises: listed and measured, not final, and a correction after settling shows as Revised. After the scan ends nothing changes again.

Implements M2's settled-figure capture. Row gains SettledBytes/SettledOnDisk, captured via Settle() when pending reaches 0 (FolderExited, or Seed for file rows). It also gains a Revised latch that Build sets when state is Done and the figures differ from the settled pair. The latch is published through the one TopLevelRow construction site. Remarks updated. Moved is unchanged.
Adds `TopLevelState.Done when row.Revised => "{Name}  (revised)"` before the fall-through, and a summary sentence on what the mark means.

Adds four hand-driven tracker facts for C-001 to C-004, run through a HandDriven rig over a hand-built ScanStore. The shared watcher (AssertSnapshotsHold) now also checks Revised on every real scan in the class: only on Done, set when a settled figure moved, never cleared, never on an uncorrected row. The in-place-correction fact now asserts that 1-folder is Revised and 2-folder is not.

The acceptance fact is left unchanged. Adds the C-005 negative control on a real scan that corrected nothing, the C-007 TitleOf matrix over every state with Revised both ways (rows built through the internal ctor by reflection), and the C-008 window test (RefreshTopLevel and ShowFinalTopLevel on real, never-shown MainWindows, reading the realised ListBoxItem text). Also adds the C-010 determinism fact: 20 fresh repro trees, each Done and Revised.

Replaces the three SL-063 rules the design appended with two. One says only TopLevelTracker.cs sets Revised: `\bRevised\s*=(?![=>])` over src/FsAnalyser.*/**/*.cs. The other says only TopLevelRowText.cs reads `.Revised` in the App.

Design-as-built record, following the house practice (SL-056 and others). It holds M1's structural-order reason in place of must-verify #2 and the AfterFolder fallback, and drops 'charging is deterministic'. It also holds M4's no-lock/single-thread correction, m4's restated key decision 5 (3.0% labelled folder-level), the rules, the case-to-test map and what was measured.

obligations.how: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-063-DoneRowFinality/SL-063-DoneRowFinality.Tests.csproj` now exits 0 with 10 passed, 0 failed. Before the change it exited 1 with the recorded NotEqual failure at line 66. The acceptance fact itself is unchanged.

There is no lock. The tracker is single-threaded by construction: see its remarks, and Scanner.Correct and Credit call _owner.Check(). With M2 adopted, the Done check doesn't happen in Moved at all: Build compares the row's figures with those captured on the same thread when pending reached 0. So whoever sets the mark knows the row was Done. This is proved by the four hand-driven tracker facts and by the watcher invariant across all 22 TopLevelTests.

The order is structural: Scanner.Execute runs SizeFiles, the only path to Correct, then Credit(inPlace), then Moved, only after the listing loop has emptied _pending. DoneRowFinalityTests.TheCorrectionLandsAfterTheRowSettledInEveryRun builds 20 fresh repro trees, and all 20 runs gave Done at 4 MiB with Revised true. Each tree must be fresh because a scan's probe refreshes the stale name's directory entry. Measured: 1,048,576 before a scan and 67,108,864 after, and a rescan of the same tree corrected nothing.

C-001: TopLevelTests.ANonZeroCorrectionOfADoneRowMarksItRevisedForTheRestOfTheScan (Theory over completed true/false). Row a is Done at 1 MiB, then Moved +63 MiB gives Done, 64 MiB, Revised. Moving it back to the settled figure keeps the mark, and both endings keep it. Passes.

C-002: TopLevelTests.ACorrectionOfARowStillReadingDoesNotMarkIt. Row b is Reading because b\sub is still pending. Moved +63 MiB leaves it Reading, not Revised. After b\sub is listed it settles Done at 64 MiB, still not Revised, and stays so at Finish. Passes.

C-003: TopLevelTests.ACorrectionOfADoneRowMarksItOnlyWhenAFigureMoved. Moved(0,0) on a Done row rebuilds and republishes it (asserted NotSame) and leaves it unmarked. Moving (0,4096) or (100,0) alone does mark it. Passes.

C-004: TopLevelTests.AChargeMovingBetweenTwoDoneRowsMarksBoth. Both rows are Done; row a gets Moved -1 MiB and row b +1 MiB, and both are Revised in the final snapshot. The rows still add up to the totals. Passes.

C-005: DoneRowFinalityTests.ADoneRowNothingCorrectedStillReadsItsBareName. A real scan in which no store entry is flagged ProbeCorrected (asserted); every row is Done, not Revised, and its title is exactly its name. Passes. A deliberate mutation confirmed the converter tests bite.
C-006 is the unchanged acceptance fact ADoneRowCorrectedInPlaceAfterItSettledReadsDifferentlyFromItsBareName. It now passes: the title is "1-folder  (revised)".

C-007: DoneRowFinalityTests.TheMarkShowsOnlyOnADoneRow, a Theory over all 6 TopLevelStates, with rows built through the internal ctor by reflection and Revised set both ways. Done with true gives "a-row  (revised)" and Done with false gives "a-row". Every other state gives its own existing suffix whatever the flag says. 6/6 pass.

C-008: DoneRowFinalityTests.TheResultsListShowsTheMarkOnATickAndAtTheEnding. It uses a real repro scan and two real MainWindows that are never shown. One is driven through the tick path (private _progress set, then RefreshTopLevel), the other through ShowFinalTopLevel. The list is laid out and each realised row's first TextBlock is read. Both give 1-folder "1-folder  (revised)" and 2-folder "2-folder". A mutation that drops the converter case made this test fail, so it reads rendered text.

C-010: DoneRowFinalityTests.TheCorrectionLandsAfterTheRowSettledInEveryRun, 20 fresh copies of the repro tree, 20/20 Done and Revised. It passes, and the structural reason is recorded in docs/design/SL-063-done-row-revised.md.

M2 adopted as decided. SettledBytes/SettledOnDisk are captured when pending reaches 0 (FolderExited, or Seed for file rows). Build derives Revised from state==Done && figures != settled and latches it on the Row. Moved sets nothing. Mutation checks bite: dropping the settle capture failed 14 TopLevelTests, and removing the latch failed both C-001 rows.

The rule 'only the tracker's Moved path sets the revision bit' is replaced by 'only the tracker sets a top-level row's Revised flag' over src/FsAnalyser.*/**/*.cs, excepting only TopLevelTracker.cs. The pattern is `\bRevised\s*=(?![=>])` rather than the literal `\bRevised\s*=` (see deviations). Planting violations in a scratch tree run through the engine's Fitness showed it fires on `{ Revised = r.Revised }` in Core and `{ Revised=true }` in App. It does not fire on the converter's `when row.Revised =>` or on `== true`.

The TitleOf state × Revised matrix is in the SL-063 bug project (TheMarkShowsOnlyOnADoneRow). The `\.Revised\b` rule over src/FsAnalyser.App/**/*.cs, excepting TopLevelRowText.cs, is added and fires on planted reads in WindowReport.cs and elsewhere. The binding half is tested in behaviour, not only read: TheResultsListShowsTheMarkOnATickAndAtTheEnding renders both window paths.

Rules 1 (the '(revised)' wording) and 3 (WindowReport 'Revised') are deleted and replaced by the one structural `\.Revised\b` App rule. That rule covers a duplicated suffix and the report alike, and a later report slice widens its except list on purpose.

Key decision 5 is restated in docs/design/SL-063-done-row-revised.md ('Why nothing is marked in advance'). Predictive marking is out because the acceptance asks for after-the-fact marking, 'make Done immutable' is recorded as impossible, and since SL-056 holding Done back would hold every row until the probe pass ends. The 3.0% is labelled folder-level (932,531 Done folders), and the MS hard-links citation is limited to what it says.

deviations: The Core-side rule pattern is `\bRevised\s*=(?![=>])`, not the decided literal `\bRevised\s*=` (M3). The literal matches the design's own converter case `TopLevelState.Done when row.Revised =>` in TopLevelRowText.cs, which that rule does not except, so the decided rule and the decided converter code contradict each other. The lookahead lets through only `==` and `=>`, which read the flag, and follows the precedent of SL-056's `=(?!=)` rule. Plants show it still fires on `{ Revised = x }` and `Revised=true`.

The suffix is "Name  (revised)" with two spaces, where the contract wrote "{row.Name} (revised)" with one. Every existing suffix in TitleOf uses two spaces, and the design's own stated reason for the wording was consistency with them.

The rewritten TopLevelState.Done doc says a Done row can move through any in-place probe correction, not 'only through a hardlink recharge' as the design put it. Scanner.Correct credits a correction whenever the handle's sizes differ from the listing's, which includes a file another process was writing (U-018). The mark is derived from the figures, so it covers every cause.

The design's 'written under the same lock/publish discipline Moved already uses' and 'the same lock Moved already uses' were wrong: no lock exists. The tracker is single-threaded by construction (Scanner's _owner.Check()), as the M4 override recorded. No synchronisation was added.

Per the M2 decision, Moved sets nothing and the design's 'revision bit set inside TopLevelTracker.Moved' does not exist: the flag is derived in Build from figures captured when pending reached 0. This is listed for traceability; it is the person's accepted fix, not the builder's choice.

The design record the M1 and m4 decisions say to amend was written as docs/design/SL-063-done-row-revised.md, following this repo's design-as-built practice. .taad/slices/SL-063/design-slice-1.json is another stage's own account and was left untouched.
not_built: No revision mark in the folder tree. The design's open question (tree coverage) stays open for a person. Note that a Completed scan replaces the results list with the tree (measured: the published exe's report on the repro tree shows FolderTree visible and TopLevelList with 0 realised rows). So the mark is visible only while a scan runs (in practice the probe pass) and after a Cancel.

No change to the --report schema 1 and no FsaWindowHook mode, as designed, because spike report-captures-mid-scan-done-row was no-go. Window-level proof is the in-process MainWindow test (C-008), not the shipped report.
No test for C-009 (a correction landing in the same ~250 ms interval the row first became Done). It is non-material and the design accepts it as over-marking; the settled capture marks such a row.
follow_ups: Person decision still open: should folder-tree nodes carry a revision mark? On a completed scan the tree replaces the list, so today the mark never appears after a successful ending. On a small tree (the repro finished in 23 ms) it is never on screen at all.
Wording '(revised)' versus '(updated)' or '(corrected)' is still unsettled cosmetics. It is changed in one place, TopLevelRowText.TitleOf, and TheMarkShowsOnlyOnADoneRow's InlineData.
The `\.Revised\b` App rule misses a property-pattern read such as `row is { Revised: true }`. A `\bRevised\b` pattern with the same exception would close that gap.

An Unreadable top-level row whose partial listing is later probe-corrected moves its figures with no mark, because the design scoped the mark to Done. Worth a decision if Unreadable rows are meant to read as settled too.

Measured at build, relevant to criterion 6 and SL-056: a scan's metadata probe through a stale hardlink name makes NTFS refresh that name's directory entry. `dir` showed stale.bin at 1,048,576 before a scan and 67,108,864 after, and a second scan corrected nothing. It is not a timestamp change as far as observed, but the scan does alter what the next listing sees. Any test using the stale-name shape needs a fresh tree per run.

If window-level proof through the shipped exe is ever wanted, the smallest step is an aggregate revised-row count in the report (no names, per Q-016) plus a hook mode that reports before EndingShown, as the risk spike found.

tests.note: Baseline before any change: exit 1, Assert.NotEqual failure at line 66 ('1-folder'), the recorded bug reproduced.
After the fix: exit 0, 10 passed, 0 failed (the acceptance, the control, 6 matrix rows, the window test and the 20-run determinism test). Final run took 7 s.

22 passed, including the four new tracker facts and the Revised invariants added to the shared watcher.

tests.command: same TopLevelTests filter, with the FolderExited settle capture disabled
tests.note: Deliberate mutation, since reverted: 14 of 22 failed, and the watcher invariant caught it on every real-scan test.

tests.command: same TopLevelTests filter, with Revised computed without the latch
tests.note: Deliberate mutation, since reverted: both ANonZeroCorrection... rows failed on the 'back to the settled figure keeps the mark' assertion.
Full default suite: 381 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 26 s. Includes RuleCopiesAgreeTests over the edited fitness.yaml.
The engine's own Fitness: 61 rules checked, every declared rule holds. The system python 3.14 lacked PyYAML, so the machine's existing 3.13, which has it, was used. Nothing was installed.

Scratch tree holding the two new SL-063 rules and planted violations. Exit 1 as intended: 4 violations, 2 per rule, on exactly the plants. No hit on the real TopLevelRowText.cs (`when row.Revised =>`) or TopLevelTracker.cs, and `== true` tripped only the reader rule. Scratch tree deleted.
AGREE: 11 facts, 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns, 46 settled entries not compared.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/publish
tests.note: Single-file self-contained exe published (139,892,376 bytes) to the gitignored artifacts/publish.

Published exe run through its real entry point in --report mode on a freshly built stale-hardlink repro tree: EXIT 0, core.status Completed, 2 files, 64 MiB. The completed scan shows the FolderTree (3 rows) and TopLevelList has 0 realised rows, so the report cannot show the suffix (spike no-go) and the list is replaced at a Completed ending.

Scratch console (deleted afterwards) that calls the public Scanner.Scan, polls ScanProgress.TopLevel every 250 ms as the window does, and titles rows through the App's TopLevelRowText. On a fresh repro tree it printed '1-folder  (revised)' for 64 MiB and '2-folder' bare. Run first on the tree the report run had already scanned, it showed 0 revised, because that scan's probe had refreshed stale.bin's entry to 67,108,864.

Real input validate used: Completed in 111.3 s with 410 polls. Of 126 rows, 119 were Done. 0 were revised in the final snapshot or in any poll, and 0 rows moved after a polled Done. This matches the spike's 0/126 and shows no false marks on real data. Validate's single post-Done row did not recur in this run.
0 warnings, 0 errors across Core, App and the bug project.
